This is the same path we walked start to finish. A developer named Jamie Pine built Voicebox, a free app that clones a voice from one short recording, speaks it back in 23 languages, and plugs into Claude so your AI can answer out loud in your own voice. Everything runs locally on your machine. Here is every step, plus the two things that tripped us up so they do not trip you up. 01 INSTALL VOICEBOX Download Voicebox from voicebox.sh and drag it into Applications. It is a small independent app, so it is not signed by Apple yet. The first time you open it, macOS will block it. Do not fight the popup. Go to System Settings, then Privacy and Security, scroll to the bottom, and click Open Anyway. That is it, it opens every time after that. If you would rather do it in one line, run this in Terminal first: sudo xattr -rd com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Voicebox.app 02 DOWNLOAD THE RIGHT ENGINE Voicebox ships seven voice engines and this is the one place people pick wrong. Only one engine both clones a voice from a sample and covers all 23 languages: Chatterbox Multilingual. Ai Actionable AI T H E A C T I O N A B L E A I. C O M A C T I O N A B L E A I · T H E A C T I O N A B L E A I. C O M Clone Your Voice And Give It To Your AI, Free And Local The exact setup we used to clone a voice in one recording, speak it in 23 languages, and wire it into Claude so your AI talks back to you in your own voice. All of it runs on your own Mac, nothing in the cloud. → The one engine inside Voicebox that actually clones a voice and does all 23 languages → The recording trick that decides whether your clone sounds alive or dead flat → The single command that lets Claude speak its answers back to you in your voice Open the Models tab and download Chatterbox Multilingual. Wait for it to finish before you generate anything. If you use the default engine instead, cloning either falls back to a generic voice or fails outright. Chatterbox Multilingual is the one that does the magic. 03 CLONE YOUR VOICE Go to Profiles, click New Profile, name it, and set the engine to Chatterbox Multilingual. Then record or upload one clean sample of your voice, 15 to 30 seconds is plenty. Save it and the clone is ready in seconds. The part nobody tells you The clone copies HOW you talk, not just how you sound. If you record your sample reading flat and careful, every single output comes out flat and lifeless. We learned this the hard way. Record your sample with real energy, like you are telling a friend something exciting. Smile while you do it, let your pitch move around. Whatever emotion you put into the sample is the emotion you get back. 04 SPEAK IN ANY LANGUAGE Type any text, pick your profile, and generate. Here is the one thing to understand: the language selector does not translate your words, it only sets the accent and pronunciation. So to speak real Spanish in your voice, you first put Spanish text in the box, then set the selector to Spanish. The easy way is to let your AI do the translating for you. Ask Claude to translate your line, paste the result into Voicebox, switch the selector to match, and generate. Now it is genuinely your voice speaking fluent Spanish, Japanese, or German, not English with a strange accent. One more tip: write with real punctuation. Periods, question marks, and exclamation points all change how alive the delivery sounds. 05 GIVE CLAUDE YOUR VOICE Voicebox has a built in connector so Claude Code can speak through it. With Voicebox open, run this once in Terminal to connect them: claude mcp add voicebox http://127.0.0.1:17493/mcp \ --transport http \ --header "X-Voicebox-Client-Id: claude-code" \ -s user Then open Voicebox Settings, go to the MCP tab, and bind your voice profile to the claude-code client. That tells Claude to always speak in your cloned voice instead of a default one. Voicebox has to stay open for this to work, the connector only lives while the app is running. 06 MAKE CLAUDE TALK BACK The connector only loads when a Claude session starts, so open a fresh Claude Code window. Give it any task, and add one line to your request: When you are done, use the voicebox speak tool to tell me what you did. Claude finishes the job, then your Mac reads the summary out loud in your own voice. That is the whole trick. Your AI stops being a wall of text and starts talking with you. I F A C L O N E E V E R S O U N D S F L A T It is almost always the sample, not a setting. There are no hidden emotion sliders. Re-record the sample with more energy and the output follows.
